reason: E2 directly supports laser cladding of TiAl-based coatings on TC4 and shows hardness/wear improvements, but the cited evidence uses TiAl/TiC or TiAlCu/NbC, not TiAl/WC. E1 shows WC particles improve hardness and wear resistance in a different matrix (HEA), not TiAl on TC4. E3 is about CoCrFeMnNiTi HEA and does not support the premises. The claim that beneficial TC4 properties are preserved is not directly evidenced.
premises: Laser cladding can deposit a TiAl-based composite coating on TC4
Adding WC particles to a metal matrix increases hardness and wear resistance
A TiAl matrix provides compatibility and adhesion with TC4 substrate
Dispersed hard particles in a coating reduce wear rate significantly (e.g., ~47.8%)
The composite coating will preserve beneficial properties of TC4
